full_judgment:
The plaintiff brought the suit for a declaration that the vested property proceeding as described in schedule ''Kha'' in respect of the suit land as described in schedule ''Ka'' to the plaint are collusive, fraudulent, without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The suit was fixed for peremptory hearing on 19-7-90. On that date the petitioner filed an application for adjournment on the ground that they would prefer a revision against the order passed in the Miscellaneous case No. 36 of 1990 under section 24 of the Code of Civil procedure by the District Judge, But the prayer was rejected by the learned Assistant Judge and the suit was dismissed for default. Thereafter the plaintiff preferred Title Appeal No.151 of 1990 before the District Judge, Barisal. The appeal was resisted by the defendant respondents on the ground that the appeal was not maintainable inasmuch as remedy lay under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The learned District Judge on consideration of the materials on record held that the order in question was passed under rule 8 of Order 9 of the Civil Procedure Code and, as such, the same was not appealable. Accordingly, the appeal was dismissed. 

 4. The learned appellate Court below held that the order in question is not a decree and hence not appealable. It was further observed that the order in question having been passed under rule 8 of Order 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, the same is not a decree as defined in section 2 of the Code and hence no appeal lies. The learned Advocate for the petitioner cited the case reported in AIR 1957, (Rajasthan) 11. In my opinion, the facts of that case are quite distinguishable from the facts of the present case and, as such, that case has no manner of application in the present case.
